title: Everyday symptom characterization in adult ADHD using a smartphone and activity tracker
summary:
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a disorder whose core symptoms include inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity. Clinical interviews and self-report questionnaires are used to assess the symptoms for a diagnosis. This type of symptom assessment leads to reliable diagnoses, but does not cover the entire behavior and experience of patients, as recall biases can occur, for example.
This study will therefore use various other assessment methods that can be used in everyday life to investigate the extent to which adults with ADHD and adults without ADHD differ in their symptoms, behavior and experience and physical processes in everyday life. To investigate this, two smartphone apps and an activity tracker worn on the arm will be used, which the participants will use over the course of the study. 
The smartphone app can be used to record various data, such as smartphone usage time and, for example, the brightness and volume of the surroundings, without the participants having to do anything. The activity tracker is used to measure body-related data such as movement, pulse and sleep. Furthermore, the smartphone app is used to send several daily and weekly queries to test participants regarding their perception of ADHD symptoms. The study begins with a clinical-psychological diagnostic, after which the smartphone apps are installed and the activity tracker is issued. The data is collected over a period of 14 days.

Adult patients with ADHD in whom the following parameters are assessed over a period of 14 complete days using two smartphone apps and an activity tracker (EmpaticaEmbrace Plus):

Initial assessment only:
- Demographic questionnaire (self created)
- Brief Diagnostic Interview for Mental Disorder

See parameters listed in Arm 1.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The following inclusion criteria apply to the ADHD group:
- Current diagnosis of ADHD according to DSM-V or ICD-10
- Age between 18-55 years
- Use of an Android smartphone

The following inclusion criteria apply to the control group
- Age between 18-55 years
- Use of an Android smartphone
Exclusion criteria:
The following exclusion criteria apply to the ADHD group:
- Taking psychotropic medication (e.g. ADHD medication, antidepressants)
- Use of antihypertensive medication or non-topically applied long-term medication
- Seizure disorder (epilepsy) or other severe (neurological) illnesses or severe mental disorders such as schizophrenia
- pregnancy

The following exclusion criteria apply to the control group
- mental disorders
- No seizure disorders (epilepsy) or other serious (neurological) illnesses
- Taking psychotropic medication (e.g. ADHD medication, antidepressants)
- Use of antihypertensive medication or non-topically applied long-term medication
- Pregnancy
